sections.description: Full-coverage WordPress core abilities for MCP. Exposes WordPress's own native core/* abilities to MCP, plus generic options, posts, taxonomies/terms, comments and users CRUD.
sections.changelog:
1.3.7

  • Declared a type for the value property of update-option and update-post-meta. Leaving it out made core's schema validator call _doing_it_wrong() and emit three PHP warnings on every write; the abilities themselves worked. Verified with a twelve-case round trip that values are unchanged either way -- a numeric string stays a string, arrays survive, escapes are untouched.

1.3.6

  • WordPress 7.1 compatibility: verified against 7.1 — nothing the plugin calls was removed or deprecated, and no ability needed adapting.
  • Fixed get-site-health-summary, which failed outright on any site whose plugins register Site Health tests as callables instead of strings (WooCommerce registers eleven of them that way). Tests are now resolved the way core's own runner does.

1.3.5

  • New defense layer: patch-post and update-post now call a wp_core_mcp_pre_content_write filter before writing the content field, letting other installed bridges refuse a write that would desynchronize a Gutenberg block's JSON attributes from its rendered HTML (this bridge has zero built-in knowledge of any specific block type — the check comes entirely from whichever bridge registers a callback). A new force_unsynced_blocks parameter (default false) opts out when the mismatch is intentional; dry_run reports the same as a non-blocking warning.

1.3.4

  • Fixed the MCP Adapter's execute-ability tool masking schema errors as a generic "Permission denied": 8 permission callbacks (comments, posts, revisions, users) now return a clear WP_Error when the expected id parameter is missing or invalid, instead of silently defaulting to 0.
  • Fixed a real bug found during regression testing: permission_restore_revision's stale bool return type caused a TypeError once its delegate could return WP_Error.

1.3.3

  • Security audit: closed a status-field privilege escalation in create-post/update-post (a Contributor could bypass the publish_posts capability via status:publish/private/future). status is now a fixed enum (draft|pending|publish|private|future) and never accepts trash — use delete-post, which has its own confirm+capability gate.
  • future status now requires a genuinely future date, verified server-side (WordPress silently downgrades a non-future future status to an immediate publish, which would otherwise be a second bypass).
  • update-option's writable whitelist narrowed: siteurl and home removed entirely (not just confirm-gated), since a wrong value can make the whole site unreachable through the web layer with no recovery path via this API. Still readable via get-option/list-options. admin_email now requires confirm: true.

1.3.2

  • CRITICAL: fixed a data-corruption bug — writes to posts, post meta, terms, comments, users, user meta, nav menus and media uploads were not wp_slash()-ed before being passed to WordPress core functions that expect slashed data, causing WordPress's own unslash step to strip literal backslashes from content (e.g. JSON-escaped characters inside Gutenberg block attributes). Fixed at 9 call sites across create/update/patch-post, update-post-meta, upload-media, create/update-term, create/update-user, create-comment, create-menu and add/update-menu-item.
  • patch-post's integrity_verified field now re-reads the actual database value after writing and compares it byte-for-byte to what was intended, instead of trusting a pre-write computation.

1.3.1

  • Initial public release: 59 abilities covering options, posts (including revisions and a surgical patch-post find/replace verb), taxonomies/terms, comments, users, menus, block widgets, media, plugin/theme status, Site Health, cron and rewrite rules, plus native core/* ability exposure.
